title: Towards Understanding the Power and Limits of the Muon Optimizer: A River-Valley Perspective
abstract: arXiv:2606.21514v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Momentum Orthogonalized by Newton-Schulz (Muon) has emerged as a promising optimizer for large language model (LLM) training, yet when and why it outperforms established alternatives such as AdamW remain insufficiently understood. This gap matters in practice, as a sub-optimal choice of optimizer or even hyper-parameters can slow progress throughout expensive pre-training and waste substantial computational resources. Existing theories largely adopt a local-improvement perspective, emphasizing singular-value flattening or implicit curvature adaptation, but they neither determine which optimizer is preferable nor explain why Muon is typically fast only during early training. To better explain Muon's complicated behavior over the entire training trajectory, we develop a trajectory-level characterization of Muon dynamics based on a new mixed-spectrum matrix sensing (MSMS) model motivated by the river-valley view of LLM loss landscapes.

translated_title: 迈向理解Muon优化器的能力与极限：河谷视角
translated_abstract: 基于Newton-Schulz正交化的动量优化器（Muon）已成为大型语言模型（LLM）训练中一种有前景的优化器，但它在何时以及为何优于AdamW等成熟的替代方案仍缺乏充分理解。这一认知缺口在实践中至关重要，因为优化器甚至超参数的次优选择可能会在整个昂贵的预训练过程中拖慢进展并浪费大量计算资源。现有理论大多采用局部改进的视角，强调奇异值平坦化或隐式曲率自适应，但它们既无法确定哪种优化器更优，也无法解释为什么Muon通常只在训练早期表现较快。为了更好地解释Muon在整个训练轨迹上的复杂行为，我们基于一种新的混合谱矩阵感知（MSMS）模型，发展了对Muon动力学的轨迹级刻画，该模型受LLM损失景观河谷视角的启发。
tldr: 该论文从河谷视角出发，基于新的混合谱矩阵感知（MSMS）模型建立了Muon优化器动力学的轨迹级刻画，以理解其在整个训练过程中相对于AdamW等优化器的优势与局限。
en_tdlr: This paper develops a trajectory-level characterization of Muon optimizer dynamics based on a new mixed-spectrum matrix sensing (MSMS) model, adopting a river-valley perspective to understand its power and limits compared to optimizers like AdamW throughout the entire training trajectory.
